classification.difficultyReason: Prepare a usable right triangle by subtracting the person's height or using roof symmetry to halve the span, then select and rearrange a trigonometric ratio.

content.prompt: For each question, solve for the unknown value.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the length of the ladder to the nearest cm.

spec.description: Ladder against a vertical wall; decorative brickwork and ladder rungs omitted.
spec.mathematics: The ladder is the hypotenuse; the horizontal adjacent side is 165 cm and the ground angle is 75 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No supplied answer appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ be the ladder length in cm.
$$\begin{align*}\cos75^\circ&=\frac{165}{L}\\L\cos75^\circ&=165\\L&=\frac{165}{\cos75^\circ}\\L&\approx638\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the horizontal distance of the person from the birds, to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Bird and person silhouettes replaced by editable role labels; both heights, dashed projections and right-angle marks retained.
spec.mathematics: The sight-line angle at the person's viewing level is 62 degrees. Birds are 2450 cm above ground and viewing level is 187 cm above ground; d is the horizontal ground distance.
spec.answerVisibility: No height difference or distance answer is supplied.

answer.worked:
The height difference is $2450-187=2263\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan62^\circ&=\frac{2263}{d}\\d\tan62^\circ&=2263\\d&=\frac{2263}{\tan62^\circ}\\d&\approx1203.3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The slant height of the roof, to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Symmetric roof triangle with both base angles, full-span dimension, dashed altitude and external right-slope dimension; decorative chimney omitted.
spec.mathematics: Both base angles are 40 degrees, the full span is 1600 cm, and w is the right sloping side.
spec.answerVisibility: The half-span and slant-height answer are not supplied.

answer.worked:
The equal base angles make the roof triangle isosceles, so the altitude bisects the span: $1600\div2=800\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos40^\circ&=\frac{800}{w}\\w\cos40^\circ&=800\\w&=\frac{800}{\cos40^\circ}\\w&\approx1044.3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The angle of the gate diagonal, to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Rectangular gate and rising diagonal; decorative posts and hinges omitted.
spec.mathematics: Width 2500 mm, height 1250 mm; theta is between the diagonal and top edge at the upper-right vertex. Top-left right-angle marker retained.

children.label: e
children.prompt: The angle of the leaning water tower, to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Unshaded leaning tower outline with ground, dashed vertical projection, right-angle mark and horizontal offset. The source's unattached 90 m label remains between the projection and leaning side.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal offset is 3 m; theta is the acute angle between the leaning side and leftward horizontal ground. The segment measured by 90 m is unresolved.

answer.worked:
If $90\text{ m}$ is the vertical height:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta&=\frac{90}{3}\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{90}{3}\right)\\\theta&\approx88^\circ5'\end{align*}$$
If $90\text{ m}$ is the leaning length:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{3}{90}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{90}\right)\\\theta&\approx88^\circ5'\end{align*}$$
Both interpretations give the supplied answer to the nearest minute.
